problem: Says the centralized scheme costs 'two messages per entry'. Standard textbook counting includes the release message, so the usual figure is three messages per entry (request, grant, release). A student writing 'two' can lose marks against a key that says three.
fix: Centralized: one coordinator grants permission. That is a request and a grant, plus a release when the process leaves, so three messages per entry in the usual count. The coordinator is a single point of failure.

problem: 'but only one machine is affected' is unclear: the crashed coordinator is one machine, but the effect is that every process is blocked, so the sentence can be misread.
fix: In the centralized scheme a coordinator crash blocks all entries until a new coordinator is elected; the failure is localized to one machine but the stall is system-wide. In the token ring a lost token stalls the whole ring until the token is regenerated, so the failure is spread out and recovery needs ring-wide detection.

problem: n appears in 'a vector V of n counters' without being defined at that point.
fix: Each process keeps a vector V of n counters, where n is the number of processes in the system, one counter per process.
